'''Kark''' was a strong expletive used by many species throughout the galaxy. It was very fluid and could be used as a derogatory modifier or as a standalone word.

==History==
The word "kark" originated at least some time before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and carried over from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

===The Clone Wars ([[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]])===
During the conflict between the Galactic Republic and a large [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist movement]] known as the Clone Wars, the word "kark" was used frequently. It was used by [[Jos Vondar]], the [[chief medical officer]] of [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit 7]] when there was explosion on the [[MedStar-class frigate/Legends|MedStar-class frigate]], where [[Tolk le Trene]], the woman he was in love with, was currently stationed. He also used it later when thinking of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Drongar/Legends|Drongar]]. [[Den Dhur]], a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] journalist, used the word upon realizing grimly that [[TDL-501 unipod waitress droid|''Teedle'']], a waitress [[Droid/Legends|droid]] and a friend of his, had donated an essential component of hers to repair the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] around the base, saving the lives of all the inhabitants.

===The DS-1 Orbital Battle Station ([[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]&mdash;[[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]])===
It was used aboard imperial [[prisoner transport]] ''[[GLTB-3181]]'' by an [[Unidentified Bakuran prisoner|unidentified]] [[Bakuran]], expressing that he did not know "whatever the kark" the Empire was [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|creating]] with very large orders of components he'd heard about. Later, in the NCO cantina of the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Steel Talon/Legends|''Steel Talon'']], the term was used by [[Olzal Erne]] expressing incredulity when he was beaten by [[Tenn Graneet]]. In the burned out [[Soft Heart Cantina]] on the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station, otherwise known as the Death Star, [[Memah Roothes]] used the term as a curse, realizing that her cantina had been the target of arson for an insurance payout. [[Kornell Divini]] used the term while thinking of the Clone Wars aboard the Death Star. [[Nova Stihl]] said it, meaning "forget it," when he was wondering who could have escaped from [[Detention Block AA-23/Legends|Detention Block AA]] on [[Deck 5]]. He concluded that he'd know them when he saw them. [[Villian Dance]], a former [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] pilot, thought "What the kark" when an order suddenly came down to stop their practice drills and set their ships' guns to combat mode. His squadron, as well as others were sent to destroy the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]] ''[[Fortressa]]'', a part of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic's]] [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]]. [[Celot Ratua Dil]], a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]], used this term when the Empire [[Destruction of Despayre|tested]] the Death Star's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] on his old home of [[Despayre]]. Stihl once again used the term when a group of prisoners escaped from Detention Block-AA 23. He, once again, had no idea who to look for or what to expect, so he resigned himself to the assumption that he'd know them when he saw them. Just after the Death Star was [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroyed]] by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], Dance used the term again, after he defected to the Alliance following the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|Destruction of Alderaan]], while trying to stabilize an ambulance that was caught in the shockwave of the battle station's explosion.

===Galactic Federation of Free Alliances ([[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]])===
It was still in use during the time of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], a galactic government, and the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] used the term "karking" to describe the shields raised to keep starfighter squadrons restrained during the [[Battle of Tralus (Second Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Tralus]]. During the same battle, her mother, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], used the same term telling [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] that it would be a "karking shame" if his own daughter, [[Syal Antilles]] shot him down as they were fighting on opposite sides. Later that year, [[Alema Rar]] encountered [[Tiz]], a member of the [[Galactic Alliance Guard]], while she was having an intimate moment with her [[Tiz's companion|fellow trooper]], the latter of which yelled this term at the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] when the pair noticed her. In the [[41 ABY|following year]], Han Solo, the father of Jaina, used the term suggesting to the people around him that they "get the kark" off [[Uroro Station]] before the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances [[Super-class Star Destroyer|''Super''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Megador]]'' destroyed it.

===After the Sith-Imperial War ([[130 ABY]]&mdash;[[137 ABY]])===
[[130 ABY|130 years]] after the Death Star I was destroyed, the term was still in use. [[Cade Skywalker]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], used it to describe enemy Imperial pilots flying [[Predator-class fighter|''Predator''-class fighters]] in the aftermath of the [[Massacre at Ossus]]. It was later used twice during the [[Skirmish on Vendaxa]], first as a derogatory standalone word by [[Deliah Blue]] and second, again, by the same Skywalker, uttering the phrase "kark it" when Deliah urged him to cut their losses and flee the fight. [[Vax Potorr]], during the [[Battle of Borosk (137 ABY)|Battle of Borosk]], exclaimed "kark me" upon stepping on a [[Mine/Legends|mine]] while distracted by gun emplacements before it exploded, killing him. Cade, while having a vision in the [[Jedi Academy (Ossus)|Jedi Academy]] on the planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], said this phrase in defiance to his ancestor, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], appearing to him as his Sith Lord identity, Darth Vader, when the latter began lecturing him about his destiny. After his vision subsided, Skywalker then said "karking" to Jedi Master [[K'Kruhk]] while the [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]], whom he assumed was a vision brought on by having just used [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]], was healing him of a stab wound he received from his visionary duel with Vader as well as toxins from [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]] he had just taken. Two weeks later, he used the variation "karking" to describe the job of taking care of and defending [[Jedi artifact/Legends|Jedi artifacts]] at the temple as [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]]. He then again used the term during a fight with his former Master, [[Wolf Sazen]], saying that he sounded just like [[Kol Skywalker]], his father, when the Zabrak told him that "we take what we are given," something Kol told Cade just before he died in the Massacre at Ossus. A member of [[1st Imperial Center Core Defense Squadron|Skull Squadron]] used the term after they lost track of the [[Mynock/Legends|''Mynock'']], Cade Skywalker's ship, in the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Skywalker, in turn, later used the word while [[Duel in the Temple of the Sith|fighting]] [[Darth Talon]] in the [[Sith temple/Legends|Sith Temple]], complaining to her that, after he faked his death at Ossus, he was outside of the struggle between the Sith and the scattered Jedi but everyone was trying to pull him back into it. Skywalker, after being captured and tortured in the temple after the duel, called [[Darth Krayt]] a "karking [[Huttese/Legends|''sleemo'']] when he infected Blue and his other friend, [[Jariah Syn]], with [[Yorik-Kul]] seeds in an attempt to force Cade to use his special healing [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]] and save them. He succeeded and three days later, Syn described Skywalker to Blue as "the karking reason we almost died" as the Sith did not care about them as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] until it was revealed that Skywalker was a former Jedi. Weeks later, after Skywalker became Talon's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] in exchange for his friends' freedom that day, Krayt wanted him to kill [[Hosk Trey'lis]], a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] Jedi Master that Skywalker had given over to the Sith several weeks earlier. Skywalker declined and Krayt killed Trey'lis himself, Cade then called the Dark Lord a "karking Sith [[Murglak/Legends|murglak]]." In the ensuing [[Skirmish at the Temple of the Sith|skrmish]] between Skywalker and Darth Krayt, who fought alongside his [[Hand (One Sith)|hands]] Darth Talon and [[Darth Nihl]]. Talon became the first casualty when Skywalker stabbed her through the abdomen, uttering the word "karkin'" to her before she fell. Just afterwards, while fighting Nihl with Krayt egging Skywalker towards killing the Sith Lord who killed his father, he told Krayt to "kark that."

==Variations==
*"Karking": A derogatory modifier.<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref><ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>
*"Kark me"<ref name="Legacy 2006 4">[[Legacy (2006) 4|''Legacy'' (2006) 4]]</ref>
*"Kark it": "Forget it"<ref name="Legacy 2006 5">[[Legacy (2006) 5|''Legacy'' (2006) 5]]</ref>
*"Kark on you!": A curse.
*"Kark up" or "karked up": Slang for 'make a mistake.'
*"Karked": Slang for "messed up".
*"What the kark"<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref><ref name="Crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> or "Whatever the kark."<ref name="Death Star novel">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>
*"Get the kark"<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>
